ai.description: This skink reaches 15 cm. It is bronze-brown with dark lateral stripes and possesses five distinct digits on each limb. It features a cylindrical body and a short, blunt snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chalcides pentadactylus* is distinguished by having exactly five digits on each limb, unlike the reduced or absent digits found in most other similar Indian skink species.
ai.habitat: The five-fingered skink inhabits arid and semi-arid sandy regions, often found in scrublands or sparse vegetation across the plains of the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Five-fingered Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and sandy substrates during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chalcides pentadactylus* is viviparous, typically giving birth to 2–4 live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chalcides pentadactylus* is found in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically within the states of Rajasthan and Gujarat at low elevations.
